title: What a packet narrative is meant to say, beside a case whose identifiers could be read into it: amounts, dates (a year, a month and day, or a month's name that is a number or a name of the case), codes, units, an NPI, a plan identifier the facts hold, another person's Social Security- or phone-shaped number, citation markers, identifier placeholders and fact tokens that spell an identifier, and a label, a placeholder and then a date; generated narratives of such pieces and of written identifiers; the browser's check
assertion: None of it is read as an identifier, and the code's own draft passes for any case whose identifiers it does not hold; the verifier flags an identifier wherever its whole-word reading or the gateway's narrative reading (`holdsNameOrNumber`, the drafter's check of its facts) holds one outside the tokens, and nowhere that neither they nor the reading across a token do; the drafter's check and the verifier read through one function; the browser's check loads neither the matcher nor the server's reading
noFileReason: Narratives are generated in memory by the property test from pieces it holds; no file.
